polish.quote: Every post page and author page is reachable by a link from the home page.
polish.why: The home page only links to authors who have at least one post, but FEAT-AUTHOR-PAGE builds a page for every author. An author with no posts has a page that nothing on the home page links to. No task or test handles this case, so the agent has to guess.
polish.fix: Reword to 'Every post page and every author page of an author with posts is reachable from the home page', or add an authors link list to the home page.

polish.why: The author page uses nothing from HomePostList; it reads only the catalog. The ordering dependency on TASK-03 is spurious, and the phrase 'depend only on' is misleading. The same applies to TASK-05.
polish.fix: Drop OWN-HOME-POST-LIST from the 'depend only on' sentence in TASK-04 and TASK-05, or note that it is an ordering dependency only.

polish.quote: sorts the posts by data.published descending
polish.why: Two posts with the same published day have no stated tie-break. Tests that compare against the content files could be flaky or disagree with the page.
polish.fix: State the tie-break: published descending, then entry id ascending (a stable sort over the id-ascending list).

polish.why: The kit schema uses z.coerce.date(), which yields a UTC-midnight Date, and the pages print toISOString().slice(0,10). 'Local' conflicts with the UTC rendering, which is only safe because of how the date is rendered.
polish.fix: Say 'calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD, rendered from the UTC date)' or tell pages to render with timeZone UTC.

polish.why: There are two body sources: the single-line frontmatter 'body' field and the markdown file body. The kit page renders both. It is not stated which one the 'shows body text' test must assert on.
polish.fix: State that the post page shows the frontmatter body field in its own element and the markdown body after it, and that the test asserts the frontmatter value.

polish.quote: No shared acceptance criterion requires the final integration and packaging gate.
polish.why: This is boilerplate that adds nothing.
The example comes from a different product (teas), and the flow-list and no-detail-route rules in the same item do not apply here. Every collection has a detail route and no list fields exist.
polish.fix: Use /posts/01-sample-entry/ as the example and drop the list-field and no-detail-route sentences for this packet.

polish.quote: need a focused way to show all posts on the home page ordered newest first without reader accounts, comments, or subscriptions
polish.why: The sentence is garbled: it restates a goal as a problem and mixes in non-goals. It is harmless but unclear.
polish.fix: Rewrite as: 'Readers cannot easily find recent posts across several writers; they need one page listing all posts newest first.'

review.verdict: No blocking defects. Every idea sentence maps to a feature with testable acceptance criteria. Task order is dependency-safe, because the kit supplies the shells and the catalog throws on an unknown author before any page uses it. The AGENTS owner map and the TASKS create/modify lists agree, the kit files named in TASKS exist, and the astro-web build and test path is coherent at each task. Only polish items remain.
